ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Cleopatra

code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 25 weeks: growth scan, glucose challenge, and blood count

text.paragraph: Prenatal visit at 25 weeks with the growth scan and glucose challenge. [S]

Cleopatra returns at 25 weeks 0 days. The gastroenteritis three weeks ago settled within two days with oral fluids, and the tightenings stopped with it; she has had none since. Both babies move often. She takes aspirin, the prenatal vitamin, and ferrous sulfate every other day. She has no headache, visual change, swelling of the face or hands, bleeding, leaking fluid, or urinary symptoms. She is still working full days but has moved most of her meetings to the mornings and rests in the afternoon. She had the growth scan and the glucose challenge this morning. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-23; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Fundal height 29 cm, consistent with twins at 25 weeks; non-tender
Scan: estimated weights 760 and 720 g, discordance 5 percent; normal fluid; fetal hearts 144 and 140 per minute

Uterus larger than dates in early pregnancy: 9 weeks by a certain last menstrual period, with the uterus about 12 to 13 weeks in size; nausea and vomiting heavier than in her first pregnancy; no bleeding; cause not yet known (multiple pregnancy, dating error, fibroids, or molar pregnancy)
S — Synthetic presenting finding anchored to the documented conception in the winter of 41 to 40 BC; it resolves when the ultrasound explains it.
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, moderate (PUQE score 9); keeping fluids down; no weight loss or ketonuria
S — Synthetic; nausea is common and often heavier in early pregnancy with a large uterus.
Iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy: hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, MCV 79 fL, ferritin 14 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding; it echoes no documented diagnosis.

Twin pregnancy, dichorionic diamniotic, second pregnancy (gravida 2, para 1): two live fetuses with a thick dividing membrane and a twin-peak (lambda) sign at 11 weeks; dated by her last period, confirmed by the crown-rump lengths
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to the documented twins of 40 BC; chorionicity is a modern finding and makes no claim about her real pregnancy.
Acute viral gastroenteritis at 22 weeks in a twin pregnancy, with mild dehydration and painless tightenings; no preterm labor (cervical length 39 mm); resolved with oral rehydration
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness at an unscheduled visit, chosen to teach the assessment of tightenings and dehydration in a twin pregnancy; it echoes no documented illness.
